logline: In a future where a mysterious entity called the Ghost saved humanity from solar extinction, two investigators across different timelines must find her before a condemned killer does - and the grid she built starts to fail.

renewal.note: Grid is a 10-episode limited series that concluded April 20, 2022. No second season was announced.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb settled at 6.4. Pierce Conran at the South China Morning Post gave it 1.5/5, arguing the show squanders its atmospheric setup once time-travel mechanics undermine narrative coherence. Rotten Tomatoes shows a 67% audience score with no formal critic count registered.

pull_quotes.text: Starts well but devolves into just another Korean time-travel mess.
pull_quotes.source: Pierce Conran / South China Morning Post

seasons.review_body: Grid premiered on Disney+ on February 16, 2022, for Asia-Pacific subscribers (Hulu in the US), running 10 episodes and concluding April 20. The concept is ambitious: a dystopian future protected by a quantum grid, two parallel-timeline investigators hunting the phantom who built it, a serial killer also in pursuit. The production values are Disney+ standard and Seo Kang-joon brings committed intensity to the lead role. The problem, identified by Pierce Conran at the South China Morning Post (1.5/5), is that the time-travel mechanics the show introduces to resolve its central mystery introduce more logical inconsistencies than they solve - a pattern familiar in Korean serialised fantasy. IMDb audiences settled at 6.4, broadly consistent with the critical read: a show that earns its first few episodes and gives back the goodwill in the final stretch.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Grid's premiere aired February 16, 2022 on Disney+ for Asia-Pacific subscribers (Hulu in the US) and was the season's strongest hour. The concept - a dystopian future protected by a quantum grid, investigators from two parallel timelines hunting the phantom who built it - was established through character observation rather than exposition, and director Kim Hwi executed the world-building with the visual atmosphere the premise required. The Ghost's first documented appearance in archive footage was the episode's structural event: the series establishing its central image - the mysterious figure who built the infrastructure that sustains civilisation and then disappeared - before beginning to unravel the implications. The premiere was consistently noted by viewers as the entry point that made continuing the series feel worthwhile, which made the later episodes' logical inconsistencies (identified by Pierce Conran at South China Morning Post as a fundamental issue with the time-travel mechanics) feel like a specific promise betrayed by a specific failure rather than a generalised disappointment.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere is the season's strongest hour. The world-building comes through character observation rather than exposition dump, and the central mystery of the Ghost is framed with genuine visual atmosphere. The episode is often treated as the entry point that makes the rest of the series feel worth continuing.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The Ghost's first documented appearance in the archive footage - the series establishing its central image before beginning to unravel it.
